title: Python: duplicate imports of the same symbol are one binding for known-class binding from an annotation (DEC-303 (a93) item 1)
description: Accepted hold task for rich misses 5.7 (rich/rule.py:66) and 5.8 (rich/table.py:491), classified under DEC-303 (a92) item 3 and ruled by (a93) item 1. Measured at dev dce9e90: a module that imports the same class name twice suppresses known-class binding from the annotation, even though both imports bind the same class; rule.py imports Console at line 3 (relative) and 118 (absolute, in its __main__ demo), table.py at 18-25 (TYPE_CHECKING) and 929 (absolute). Ruling: duplicate imports of the SAME symbol become one binding. Fixtures cover 5.7's __main__ shape and 5.8's closure read. Refused twins must still refuse: two imports binding DIFFERENT symbols, an import followed by a non-import rebinding, and a conditional import of a different symbol. Mutants observed red. Two rounds; every created and removed in-repo edge on the five-pin corpus is listed to opum-doc before the clear. Runs after GCLI-151, which is landed. ALSO CARRIED the N5 item from the #262 round-2 review (ODOC-640, opum-ai/opum-doc#2113): the 6d constructed arm checked hasReplacingDecorator but not instanceClassOf, so a C whose __new__ returns a writing descendant still resolved x = C(); x.m(). MEASURED on dev 5e9f4215 and again on d0ea6bc4, read-only: with C.__new__ returning D() and D(C).__init__ writing self.__class__ = Other, x = C(); x.m() gave app.py:C.m; the no-write twin gave C.m and the no-__new__ control gave C.m, so the with-write site was a REAL wrong edge. As built, the candidate guard (knownClassOf's call arm consulting instanceClassOf) also refused the no-write twin and removed 129 five-pin edges not shown wrong; DEC-303 (a95) therefore ruled N5 OUT of this task's PR — #264's delta after that removal is exactly the 40 created duplicate-import edges. N5 is a stated limit in the pre-registration and an item on GCLI-172, which carries the measurement; how a later fix keys its refusal is GCLI-172's design question for opum-doc.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A module that imports the same class twice (relative and absolute, in any scope) resolves an annotated receiver method call to the class method; fixtures cover the 5.7 __main__ shape and the 5.8 closure read
Two imports binding different symbols, an import followed by a non-import rebinding, and a conditional import of a different symbol all stay unresolved, with fixtures and mutants observed red
Every in-repo edge created or removed on the five-pin corpus is listed to opum-doc before the clear

plan: 1. Measure N5 read-only on dev d0ea6bc: write/no-write/no-__new__ twins over the 6d constructed arm; record the answer before building. (Done; N5 later removed from this task by DEC-303 (a95).)
2. Reproduce 5.7 (__main__ duplicate import) and 5.8 (closure read) as failing fixtures on dev. (Done.)

3. Implement duplicate imports of the SAME class as one binding in the annotation known-class path, with a per-binding check that every binding is an import resolving to the same class. N5 is not part of this task after (a95): it is a stated limit plus an item on GCLI-172.

4. Refused twins with fixtures and mutants observed red: different symbols, import then non-import rebinding, a conditional import of a different symbol, a later class binding of the name (the per-binding guard), and a function-local duplicate import (any scope).

5. Blast radius over the five pins, the 1394-source corpus and the fixture set; list every created/removed in-repo edge, report to the leader for opum-doc before the clear. Accepted delta: 40 created, 0 removed, 0 flag-changed.
6. Two rounds, one PR on a task branch off dev, CI by ref, report PR number + head SHA.
implementationNotes: N5 measured FIRST, read-only, on dev d0ea6bc4 (twins, one file): write shape (C.__new__ returns D(); D(C).__init__ writes self.__class__ = Other; x = C(); x.m()) gives app.py:C.m; the no-write twin gives C.m; both no-__new__ controls give C.m. Real pre-existing wrong edge, as the a94 ruling recorded, and removal-only by construction: the fix consults instanceClassOf in knownClassOf's call arm, which can only drop a resolution. Blast radius measured with the GCLI-161 proof kit over the five pins at dev vs the patched tree: 40 created edges (all the duplicate-import annotation fix, concentrated in rich: Console methods through parameters annotated Console, including the two named targets rich/rule.py:66 and rich/table.py:491) and 129 removed edges (all N5: classes whose __new__ may return a descendant, e.g. tqdm.std.tqdm, jinja2.environment.Template, and classes with opaque bases e.g. httpx Headers/QueryParams/Cookies). No edge is created by the N5 half. The full created/removed list is in the PR body and reported to opum-doc before the clear.

DEC-303 (a95) ruled on #264 at b2ed5577: the duplicate-import change is cleared as reported, and N5 does NOT ride. N5 is removed from #264 — the 6d arm and the two moved tests equal dev d0ea6bc4 in the diff, and the N5 fixtures are gone — because as built it also refused where nothing writes (the no-write twin) and removed 129 five-pin edges not shown wrong, spending the recall (a94) item 1 already declined at about 0.91. The N5 measurement (write shape, no-write twin, no-__new__ controls) is carried to GCLI-172 as evidence. Accepted delta for #264 after the removal, against dev d0ea6bc4: exactly the 40 created edges listed in the PR body, 0 corpus removals, 0 flag-changed. Round 1 was not spent; it runs on the new head.

Closed with landing evidence. opum-ai/glyph-cli#264 head 7c9e870f: round-2 APPROVE, CI 4/4 by ref on that SHA (run 46072274109 covering 7c9e870f), squash-merged to dev; origin/main unchanged at dad914a3, no promotion. AC2's evidence for the two different-class twins: mutant M5 (drop the same-class compare at calls.ts:3520, so the last binding wins) observed RED on BOTH 'two imports binding DIFFERENT classes' and 'a conditional import of a DIFFERENT class' on the landed tree, with the same tests green unmutated; M1, M2 and M4 are also red there. Two records notes: (1) the landed squash subject and first body block still describe N5 ('the 6d arm reads instanceClassOf'), which the final diff does not contain — the tree is correct and (a95) removed N5, but dev's commit subject misdescribes it; reported to the leader, history not rewritten. (2) A non-blocking reviewer nit is carried forward, not fixed here: the calls.ts:3504-3505 doc comment says an import followed by a non-import rebinding is 'answered as rebound, never multiply', false for a class/def rebinding (which reaches the helper and refuses per binding at 3515); the test comment at test:597-599 is right. Recorded on GCLI-171 to ride its PR or the next src change.
finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/glyph-cli#264: duplicate imports of the same class are one binding for annotation known-class binding (DEC-303 (a93) item 1), resolving rich's 5.7 (rule.py:66) and 5.8 (table.py:491), with refused-twin fixtures and mutants M1, M2, M4 and M5 observed red on the landed tree. Validated by CI 4/4 by ref in run 46072274109 covering head 7c9e870f, with round-2 APPROVE. N5 was measured on dev and ruled out of this task by (a95); it is carried to GCLI-172 as evidence and a stated limit. The trailing-star-import limit was stated per (a96) item 1. Five-pin delta: 40 created edges, 0 removed, 0 flag-changed.
